subject: Phased provisioning & pricing sensitivity for enterprise pilot -> committed tier
messages:
From: Marcus Lee <marcus.lee@pritech.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-08-26T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Pilot -> commit: request for phased start and pricing guardrails

Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency profile you showed on the conversational models is promising for our use case. We are greenlit for a 3-month pilot from our product team, but procurement is pushing for committed capacity as part of the enterprise contract once the pilot completes.

Two asks from our side as we draft internal docs: 1) can we structure the reserved capacity so the commit "start date" is phased (i.e., lower initial committed vGPU-hours for months 1–3 post-pilot, ramping to full commit by month 6)? 2) can Redwood provide a pricing cap (or cap-and-floor) tied to an agreed GPU-cost index so we have protection if cloud/GPU costs spike in year 1? Specifically, we need a comfort mechanism if underlying GPU market pricesincrease >12% quarter-over-quarter — some sort of capped pass-through or credit.

We can share our expected usage curve and have a proposed SKU mix. I attached our security questionnaire and the usage spreadsheet for context.

Can we get an initial feasibility note and a ballpark on discount tiers for a 24-month committed ARR with a 6-month phased ramp? Our legal will start redlining once procurement sees those guardrails.

Best,
Marcus
Marcus Lee
Head of Platform
PriTech

Attachments: Pritech_security_questionnaire.pdf, pritech_usage_model.csv

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marcus Lee <marcus.lee@pritech.ai>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-08-26T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot -> commit: request for phased start and pricing guardrails

Hi Marcus — thanks for the clear ask and for sending the usage sheet. We can absolutely model a phased-commit structure; that’s a pattern we’ve done with other pilot->enterprise transitions.

Quick answers:
- Phased commitment: feasible. We typically allow a lower committed base for the first 3 months post-pilot with a predefined ramp (month 4–6) to full committed capacity. That keeps predictability for both parties and reduces immediate cash pressure for customers.
- Pricing guardrail: we can offer a capped pass-through tied to an agreed GPU-cost index OR a hybrid where Redwood absorbs X% of the increase until a threshold and then passes the remainder. This usually requires an exec-level concession depending on the threshold and term.

I’m looping in Kimberly for pricing scenarios and Sean for approval path/discount authority. Kimberly — can you share 2–3 pricing options (conservative, balanced, concession) that include sku mix, initial ramp months, and a GPU-index clause? Sean — are you able to indicate how far we can go on absorbing market-driven cost increases for a 24-month commitment?

Marcus — I’ll aim to get a short feasibility note and pricing options by EOD tomorrow.

Cheers,
Naomi
Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-08-27T08:42:00-07:00
Subject: Pricing scenarios for Pritech (phased ramp + GPU index guardrail)

Naomi / Sean — attached is a short model (pricing_scenarios_sheet.xlsx) with three scenarios based on the usage sample Marcus provided:

1) Conservative: 15% discount off list for 24-month term, phased ramp (50% of committed vGPU-hours months 1–3, 75% months 4–6, 100% thereafter). GPU index clause: customer liable for full pass-through of GPU cost movement; Redwood provides a 5% buffer credit if index moves >10% in a single quarter.

2) Balanced: 22% discount, phased ramp (60/80/100), GPU index: Redwood absorbs first 8% of increase per quarter, then passes through incremental change up to a cap of +20% annually; if index exceeds +20% we offer a one-time credit equal to 50% of the overage on the next invoice (exec approval required).

3) Concession: 30% discount, phased ramp (70/90/100), GPU index: Redwood guarantees a cap of +15% annual pass-through; any exposure above that is absorbed by Redwood for the first year. Requires sign-off by Head of Sales + CFO for pricing and revenue recognition treatment.

Key assumptions are in the sheet (sku mix, effective token rates, expected sustained concurrency).

Notes: the concession option materially reduces our margin in the face of a rapid GPU price surge, so we should only deploy it for strategic references or large ARR.

Kimberly
Sr. Pricing Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: pricing_scenarios_sheet.xlsx

From: Marcus Lee <marcus.lee@pritech.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <pshah@pritech.ai>
Date: 2026-08-28T10:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot -> commit: request for phased start and pricing guardrails

Thanks Naomi / Kim — this is helpful and aligns with what our procurement team is looking for. A couple of clarifying items from procurement/legal: 1) they prefer the Balanced option but would like the cap to be explicitly written as a formula ("Redwood pass-through = max(0, GPU_index_delta - 8%) capped at 20% annually") and 2) they want a rollback option in months 4–6 if our production volumes materially undershoot the projected usage (a one-time rebaseline with prorated committed adjustment).

Also: for the concession scenarios that require exec sign-off, could Redwood provide an escalation path and a nominal floor (e.g., minimum price per vGPU-hour) so our CFO can model worst-case cashflow?

If you can put the Balanced option into a short term-sheet with the formula and the rebaseline trigger language, we can run it through procurement next week. That would speed up legal.

Marcus

—
Marcus Lee
Head of Platform, PriTech

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-08-30T15:45:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: approval path for Balanced scenario (PRT-2026-0826)

Sean / Kim — summary of ask from PriTech: they want the Balanced scenario with the explicit formula, a rebaseline window in months 4–6, and a rollback/proration clause if usage materially undershoots. Procurement will push for a defined floor and an escalation path if GPU-index > 20% annual.

Proposed internal ask:
- Approve Balanced pricing (22% discount) conditional on:
  * Redwood absorbing first 8% GPU-index increase per quarter
  * Pass-through formula: "Redwood pass-through = max(0, GPU_index_delta - 8%) capped at 20% annual"
  * Rebaseline clause: one-time rebaseline in month 5 if actual monthly vGPU-hours < 70% of projected usage for both months 3–4; committed capacity prorated thereafter (legal to draft language)
  * Floor: set a nominal floor at $0.XX per vGPU-hour (Kim to propose exact floor in revenue impact sheet)
- If floor or cap moves beyond these parameters, escalate to Head of Sales + CFO.

Kim — can you produce the short term-sheet (1 page) with the formula and a suggested floor by tomorrow morning so I can send it to Marcus? Sean — are you comfortable with this as the default approval, or do we need exec sign-off?

Thanks — Naomi
Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
